headline: FC Dallas edges SKC 4-3 in week's wildest finish
dek: Fourteen matches across four days produced nine goals in Portland alone and a 4-4 thriller in Toronto.
body: Columbus rolled Colorado 3-0 on Sept. 5, the week's most clinical result. Orlando held San Diego 1-0 and Philadelphia turned away CF Montréal 2-0 the same night. Toronto and Chicago traded four goals apiece in a draw. FC Dallas beat Sporting Kansas City 4-3 on Sept. 6, Portland edged Minnesota 5-4, and St. Louis stunned Vancouver 3-1. Inter Miami and Atlanta drew 2-2, Real Salt Lake and LAFC shared the points 2-2, and LA Galaxy topped New England 2-1. Austin and San Jose drew 1-1, Seattle and New York held 0-0, and New York City and Nashville finished goalless on Sept. 4.

headline: Columbus, Vancouver busy as window shuts
dek: Three departures, three arrivals, and the Crew lead the league's late activity heading into the final stretch.
body: Manu García has left Sporting Kansas City after the club mutually terminated his contract; he logs 1,470 minutes this season. Reports link him to a return to Aris Thessaloniki. Hugo Cuypers departs Chicago Fire after 990 minutes in 2026, transferred to Liga MX side CF Monterrey. Chris Cappis exits FC Dallas with 1,080 minutes this season. On the inbound side, Vancouver add forward Yadaly Diaby from French Ligue 2 side Grenoble Foot 38. Columbus bring in winger Anass Zaroury on loan from Panathinaikos and Uruguayan midfielder Santiago Rodríguez.

headline: Musa and Messi locked at 18 goals apiece
dek: FC Cincinnati's Evander sits third at 14, five back, with the assist title also in play.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Leo Messi of Inter Miami CF are deadlocked at 18 goals, the league's outright leaders. FC Cincinnati's Evander trails at 14. In the assists race, Evander, Messi, and Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC are level at 10 apiece. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps leads all tacklers at 90, more than 30 clear of D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 59 and teammate João Peglow at 55. On the finishing side, Guilherme of Houston and NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández each outperform their xG by 5.8 goals. St. Louis pair Rafael Navarro and Simon Becher are the league's most prominent under-performers, down 4.3 and 3.5 goals respectively against expectation.

headline: Nashville lead East by a distance; Whitecaps top West
dek: The Eastern leader has allowed just 17 goals all season, also the best defensive record in the league.
body: Nashville SC sit atop the Eastern Conference with 53 points on a 16W-5D-2L record, 47 goals scored and 17 conceded. That goals-against total is also the best in the entire league. Vancouver Whitecaps lead the Western Conference at 43 points, record 13W-4D-5L, with 49 goals for and 21 against. Inter Miami CF hold the league's most potent attack with 58 goals scored, 11 more than the next Western side.

headline: Three depart MLS; Walta, Abu Farkhi, Modesto arrive
dek: A Utah homegrown heads to the Premier League while two clubs bring in reinforcements from Israel and Finland.
body: Real Salt Lake homegrown winger Zavier Gozo, 19, has transferred to Crystal Palace of the English Premier League after logging 1,470 minutes this season. LA Galaxy defender Miki Yamane, 32, has joined J1 League side Urawa Red Diamonds after 1,380 minutes in 2026. Nashville SC forward Woobens Pacius has moved to Ligue 3's FC Rouen 1899 after 900 minutes this season. On the incoming side, Colorado Rapids acquired Israeli forward Sayed Abu Farkhi from Maccabi Tel Aviv as a U-22 initiative signing. LAFC added Finnish midfielder Leo Walta on loan from EFL Championship side Swansea City, with a purchase option. Vancouver Whitecaps have added Rui Modesto to their roster.

headline: Musa and Messi locked at 18; Evander trails by four
dek: The top of the scoring chart is deadlocked heading into the final weeks of the regular season.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Leo Messi of Inter Miami CF each sit on 18 goals, sharing the league lead. FC Cincinnati's Evander is third at 14. Evander also shares the assists lead at 10, alongside Messi and San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer. On the defensive side, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas leads all players in tackles with 90, well clear of D.C. United teammates Silvan Hefti (59) and João Peglow (55). The most pronounced finishing outliers: Guilherme of Houston and NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández both exceed their expected goals by 5.8, while St. Louis CITY SC's Rafael Navarro trails his xG by 4.3 goals.

headline: Nashville leads East; Vancouver holds West at 43 pts
dek: Nashville's defense, the stingiest in the league, anchors a six-point cushion over the Western Conference leader.
body: Nashville SC sit atop the Eastern Conference with 53 points on a 16W-5D-2L record, having conceded just 17 goals, the fewest in MLS. They have scored 47. In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps lead at 43 points, 13W-4D-5L, with 49 goals for and 21 against. Inter Miami CF carry the league's most potent attack at 58 goals scored. Nashville's defensive record doubles as the best in the league across both conferences.

headline: D.C. United land Ordaz from LAFC in $2.375M deal
dek: The El Salvador international joins the Black-and-Red as a U22 Initiative player after 98 appearances in LAFC colors.
body: D.C. United have acquired forward Nathan Ordaz from LAFC for $2.375 million, with up to an additional $500,000 available in performance incentives. LAFC also retains a sell-on percentage on any future trade. Ordaz, 22, made 98 appearances for the Black and Gold across all competitions since signing as the club's fourth homegrown player in 2022, recording 14 goals and 12 assists. He carries 14 caps for El Salvador into his new posting in the nation's capital.

headline: Cuypers leads Musa and Messi by one at the top
dek: Chicago's Hugo Cuypers holds a slim advantage in the MLS scoring race with the season past its midpoint.
body: Hugo Cuypers of Chicago Fire FC sits first in the goals table on 13, one clear of Petar Musa (FC Dallas) and Leo Messi (Inter Miami CF), who are level on 12. Messi also ranks second in the assists race on seven, one behind LAFC's Son Heung-Min, who leads the league on eight. Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC shares second in assists with Messi on seven. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps tops the tackles leaderboard at 52, with Inter Miami's Yannick Bright second on 47 and D.C. United's João Peglow third on 45.

headline: Ingvartsen and Guilherme outrun the model by wide margins
dek: Two strikers are converting well beyond expectation, while Vancouver's Brian White carries a significant xG deficit.
body: San Diego FC's Marcus Ingvartsen leads MLS in xG outperformance with 11 goals against an xG of 6.8, a gap of plus-4.3. Houston Dynamo's Guilherme is close behind at plus-4.2, having scored eight times from an xG of 3.8. On the other side, Vancouver's Brian White sits 2.4 goals below expectation, 10 goals scored against an xG of 12.4, the largest deficit in the league. Minnesota's Kelvin Yeboah is next at minus-1.8, having hit eight from an xG of 9.8.

headline: Nashville and San Jose sit atop their conferences
dek: Nashville's backline remains the stingiest in the league as San Jose pace the West on goal difference.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference on 33 points, built on a 10W-3D-1L record. Their 11 goals allowed is the best defensive mark in MLS. San Jose Earthquakes top the West on 32 points at 10W-2D-3L, having scored 34 times in 15 outings. Inter Miami CF hold the league's most potent attack with 39 goals scored, seven more than any conference leader, though their table standing trails Nashville's in the East.

headline: Six players cross MLS borders in one window
dek: Gabriel Pirani heads to San Diego FC while two departures shrink the Galaxy and Whitecaps rosters.
body: Gabriel Pirani moves from D.C. United to San Diego FC. On the departure side, Gabriel Pec leaves LA Galaxy having logged 1,260 minutes this season, and Aziel Jackson exits Vancouver Whitecaps with 1,080 minutes on his ledger. Their destinations are unknown. Three arrivals offset the losses elsewhere: Yevhen Cheberko joins LAFC, Curtis Ofori signs with Red Bull New York, and Nate Edwards links up with Toronto FC.
